requirement: Obtain a Clean Air Act (CAA) permit under Section 328 of the CAA for the construction and operation of an offshore windfarm, including export cables, on the Outer Continental Shelf (OCS).
scope: Construction and operation of offshore windfarm on the OCS, including export cables.
related_domains: air quality; environmental permitting; offshore construction; offshore operation

requirement: Obtain a Title V operating permit.
scope: Operation of offshore windfarm.
related_domains: air quality; environmental permitting; offshore operation

requirement: Permit must contain all applicable requirements under 40 C.F.R. part 55.
scope: Offshore windfarm permitting.
related_domains: environmental permitting; regulatory compliance

requirement: Construction and operations plans from wind energy developers must be submitted to and reviewed by the Bureau of Ocean Energy Management (BOEM) for approval or disapproval.
scope: Offshore wind energy projects
related_domains: permitting; project development; regulatory compliance

requirement: The OCS permit applicant then follows the procedural requirements to obtain a federal permit as outlined in 40 C.F.R. part 124. The applicant submits an air permit application that provides the information to show that it will comply with all applicable federal requirements, including those requirements found in 40 C.F.R. part 55 (which, because of the consistency update, include certain state and local requirements incorporated by reference into federal law), and any other federal standard that may apply to the source.
scope: OCS permit applicants for offshore wind farms; air permit application process; construction and operation phase
related_domains: air quality control; permitting; environmental compliance

requirement: The pollutant-emitting activities within the WDA are part of a single plan to construct and operate an offshore windfarm and can be viewed as a single facility that meets the definition of an OCS source in § 55.2.
scope: Wind Development Area (WDA) facility; offshore windfarm
related_domains: regulatory classification; permitting; offshore development

requirement: permit that meets the CAA requirements
scope: Offshore wind farm construction and permitting
related_domains: environmental compliance; permitting

requirement: The emission units on the service fleet vessel are still subject to the permit’s NNSR offset requirements once the service fleet vessel is no longer meeting the criteria for an OCS source.
scope: Emission units on service fleet vessels
related_domains: Air quality; Environmental regulation; Permitting

requirement: In the case of a safety issue, engine failure, or a storm at sea that requires a vessel to temporarily attach itself to the seabed, the vessel will not be considered an OCS source because the vessel during this time is not considered to be erected on the seabed for the purposes of exploring, developing, or producing resources therefrom.
scope: Vessels temporarily attached to the seabed due to safety issue, engine failure, or storm at sea
related_domains: Jurisdictional boundaries; Vessel operations; Regulatory applicability

requirement: A construction and operation plan that allows for the construction and operation of WTGs and ESPs, and equipment on those platforms, must be submitted to and approved by BOEM to demonstrate the platforms are authorized under the OCSLA (43 U.S.C. § 1331 et seq.).
scope: Construction and operation of WTGs and ESPs on the Outer Continental Shelf (OCS)
related_domains: permitting; regulatory compliance; offshore development

requirement: Engines on a vessel are considered stationary sources and not nonroad engines when the engines are operating while the vessel meets the definition of an OCS source.
scope: Vessels operating while meeting the definition of an OCS source (e.g., for offshore wind projects like Vineyard Wind OCS Project)
related_domains: environmental regulation; air emissions; source classification; vessel operations

requirement: modeling for sources subject to a comprehensive plan approval
scope: construction phase of the OECLA; sources subject to a comprehensive plan approval
related_domains: environmental impact assessment; air quality; permitting

requirement: emissions must not impact any area where the applicable increment is known to be violated.
scope: temporary source (construction emissions for WDA facility and OECLA)
related_domains: air quality; environmental impact assessment; permitting

requirement: the emissions must not impact any Class I area.
scope: temporary source (construction emissions for WDA facility and OECLA)
related_domains: air quality; environmental impact assessment; permitting; protected areas

requirement: A Guideline specifies a two-tier screening approach for long-range transport assessments related to air quality impacts from construction emissions at Class I areas.
scope: Air quality impacts related to construction emissions for the WDA facility and OECLA at Class I areas; long-range transport assessments.
related_domains: environmental impact assessment; air quality modeling; construction emissions

requirement: Ambient air impacts for pollutants emitted from construction of the WDA facility must be below significance levels at distances relevant to Class I areas, as established by Class I area Significance Impact Levels (SILs).
scope: Construction period impacts from the WDA facility at Class I areas.
source: Class I area Significance Impact Levels (SILs)
related_domains: air quality; environmental impact assessment; construction phase

requirement: Assess air quality impacts and impairment to visibility, soils, and vegetation due to operational period emissions of the WDA facility and general commercial, residential, industrial and other growth associated with the operational period of the WDA facility.
scope: Operational period of the WDA facility (Vineyard Wind offshore project)
related_domains: environmental impact assessment; air quality; visibility; soil protection; vegetation protection

requirement: defined vessel categories to meet 40 C.F.R. part 94 Tier 2 standards.
scope: Vessels operating under the jurisdiction of the CA SIP (California State Implementation Plan)
related_domains: environmental protection; air quality; vessel operations; technical standards

requirement: the use of fuels with a flashpoint lower than 60°C is not allowed.
scope: Vessels and equipment used in offshore wind farm construction and operation
source: International Convention on the Safety of Life at Sea
related_domains: maritime safety; fuel management; fire safety

requirement: Each federal agency must work to ensure that public documents, notices, and hearings relating to human health or the environment are concise, understandable, and readily accessible to the public.
scope: Federal agencies involved in environmental permitting
source: Section 5-5(c) of EO 12898 (Public Participation and Access to Information)
related_domains: public participation; environmental justice; permitting process

requirement: Any facility with the potential to emit 50 tons per year of NOx is required to have a Title V operating permit.
scope: Facilities during operational phase with NOx emissions potential over 50 tons per year
related_domains: air quality; emissions control; permitting

requirement: Government-to-government consultation must be offered to each of the tribes.
scope: Projects requiring federal action impacting tribal interests
related_domains: tribal consultation; environmental permitting; cultural resource management
